title: Norway Maple: Ancient Norway Maples You Can Visit
meta_description: One of Europe's most-planted street trees, rarely left to grow. Riga's Zasulauks maple added a third to its waist in 34 years, to 5.34 metres.
intro: Norway maple is one of the most planted street trees in northern Europe, valued for tolerating road salt, compacted soil and bad air, and just as routinely cut back once it outgrows its spot, so an old one is what a city decided to keep. Riga's Zasulauks maple, beside a wooden tenement in the Kalnciema Quarter, measured four metres round in 1975 and 5.34 by 2009, a third of its waistline added in thirty-four years. One in Den Bosch stands on a two-metre-thick fortress bastion built in 1634. Munich protects two under a 2021 natural monument ordinance: one on Mondstrasse defines its square, the other on Herrnstrasse survives for being rare at its size among inner-city courtyards. Snap a leaf stalk and it bleeds white sap, the surest way to tell a Norway maple from the sycamore it is otherwise mistaken for.
